# Sandscram (거북이 경주)

> Sandscram is a luck-based party game for 2 to 8 people sharing one phone. Sea turtle hatchlings leave one nest together and dash for the sea while animal predators (gulls and crabs) and deep-rushing waves reshuffle the ranking. There are no controls: each player takes a turtle and cheers, and once per race anyone can use the 'Pause! Swap?' button to pause. A race takes about 15 seconds on average, which makes it a quick way to pick lunch, share out chores or decide who presents first. It is inspired by Darwin's natural selection, but luck decides the result, and starting positions are balanced so no lane has an advantage. It runs offline and is available in Korean and English.

Korean summary: 거북이 경주(영문 이름 Sandscram)는 2~8명이 휴대폰 한 대로 함께 하는 운에 맡기는 게임입니다. 한 둥지에서 함께 나온 바다거북 새끼들이 바다를 향해 같이 달리고, 갈매기와 게 같은 동물 천적, 깊이 밀려드는 파도가 순위를 바꿉니다. 조작은 없습니다. 참가자는 거북이를 한 마리씩 맡아 응원하고, 한 판에 한 번 '잠깐 멈추고! 바꿀래?' 버튼으로 경주를 잠시 멈출 수 있습니다. 한 판은 평균 15초 안팎이라 점심 메뉴 고르기, 당번 정하기, 발표 순서 정하기에 알맞습니다. 다윈의 자연선택에서 영감을 받았지만 결과는 운이 정하고, 출발 자리에 따른 유불리가 없도록 맞췄습니다. 인터넷 없이 실행되며 한국어와 영어를 지원합니다.

## Key facts
- Players: 2–8 on one phone (one turtle each); no controls, one 'Pause! Swap?' per race
- Average race: about 15 seconds (plus 3-second countdown)
- Result is luck: turtle speed varies ±4% with ~0 correlation to survival; each starting lane wins within ±2.5 percentage points of its fair share (4,000-race test)
- Ties: equal on-screen time (0.01 s) share the rank
- Platform: Android (offline). Languages: Korean, English (default turtle names in 17 languages)
- Developer: Sandscram · Contact: nowons@gmail.com

## FAQ
- **What is Sandscram?** A luck-based party game for 2 to 8 people sharing one phone. Sea turtle hatchlings leave one nest together and race to the sea, and the order they reach the water is the ranking. Gulls, crabs and deep-rushing waves reshuffle it.
- **How many people can play?** From 2 to 8. Choose 2 to 8 turtles and each person takes one. You only need one phone.
- **Do I need to control anything?** No. There are no controls; you just cheer. Once per race, until the leader is halfway across the sand, anyone can use the 'Pause! Swap?' button to pause.
- **How long is one race?** About 15 seconds on average, plus a 3-second countdown before the start.
- **Does skill or the turtle you pick affect the result?** Barely. Turtle speeds differ by only ±4%, and speed has almost no link to survival. In a 4,000-race test, every starting lane won within 2.5 percentage points of its expected share. 'More turtles together means fewer get caught' is a rule of this game, not a claim about real sea-turtle ecology.
- **What can I use it for?** Pick the lunch menu, pick who buys coffee after lunch, or decide turns or chores.
- **What happens in a tie?** If two turtles show the same time on screen (to 0.01 seconds), they share the rank. Players settle it themselves, for example with another race or rock-paper-scissors.
- **Does it need an internet connection?** No. The game runs offline. Sharing the results picture uses the connection of the app you share to.
- **How is it related to Darwin's natural selection?** It is a game of luck inspired by natural selection. Real hatchlings leave the nest in a group and run for the sea. On the beach they may meet animal predators such as gulls and crabs. The game simplifies this, and luck decides the result. Real hatchlings mostly emerge at night; the game shows daytime so the race is easy to watch.
- **Which animals appear?** Olive ridley sea turtles (Lepidochelys olivacea), ghost crabs (genus Ocypode) and gulls (Laridae), drawn in a simple style inspired by real beach ecology. With luck, they live for decades.
- **What is the ending about?** A short ending may follow the results. After making it across the beach together, risks such as ghost nets and plastic can continue in the sea. We keep animal predators (gulls and crabs) separate from trash hazards, and we do not call people or children predators. The theme is: 'They made it to the sea together. Now let’s keep the sea safe together.' Many sea animals may mistake plastic for food and swallow it.
- **Which languages are supported?** The interface is in Korean and English. Turtles are named after their shell colors, shown in 17 languages to match the device language.
- **Does it collect personal data?** The current version collects no personal data. Only settings such as sound volume are stored on the phone.
